title: Bicycle brake
prompt: A bench teaching model of the bicycle rim brake on pages 28 and 29 uses the pictured cable linkage with one first-class and one third-class brake arm. Spin turns the wheel. Squeeze rotates the second-class handle, pulls the cable and brings both blocks against the rim to slow it by friction. Release removes cable tension and lets the blocks clear the rim. See-through follows handle effort, cable tension, each arm's pivot and block contact. Preserve the source geometry. Do not substitute a disc brake, hydraulic brake or symmetric V-brake while retaining the original class labels.
blurb: A bench teaching model shows how three levers pull two brake blocks against a spinning bicycle rim.

adaptation.kind: Bench teaching model of the illustrated mixed-class side-pull linkage
limits: Scaled schematic geometry; not a production caliper specification.
Friction and wheel inertia are illustrative, not calibrated.
Cable pull is a model displacement, not measured hardware travel.
Pad faces are aligned at full squeeze.
No edition-union claim. The 1988 edition remains inaccessible and unverified.
